newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia denies S.Korea has banned its meat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia denies S.Korea has banned its meat.

text.p: The Australian government on Wednesday denied newspaper reports that South Korea had banned Australian meat and dairy products in reaction to the outbreak of anthrax in Victoria.

The reports, in the Sydney Morning Herald and the Melbourne Age newspapers, said South Korea had imposed a quiet freeze on imports of Australian meat and dairy products. The freeze had been imposed last month but kept quiet, the report said.

Denials were issued on Wednesday by Australia's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade Tim Fischer, Primary Industries Minister John Anderson, the Victorian state government Minister for Agriculture and Resources Pat McNamara and the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp.
Korean authorities were requesting "certain assurances" from Australia and were considering testing some produce from Australia, but there was no official ban, Anderson said in a statement.
"Australian officials are currently negotiating arrangements intended to minimise commercial disruption," he said.
Only three consignments of Australiabn product were being held pending final clearance, he said.
Press claims that the situation with Korea had been kept quiet were "nonsense", he said.
A number of countries in the Asia region had sought information from Australia on the anthrax outbreak, which was now well under control, and on quarantine and control measures, he said.
Australia was providing assurances and could demonstrate that its animal health and inspection controls and processes were more than adequate to ensure the safety of its produce, he said.

No meat for human consumption was being sourced from the very small area of the quarantine zone in Victoria, he said. The processes of cooling milk and pasteurisation ensured that dairy products were also sale for human consumption, he said.
Australia exports almost A$2 billion worth of dairy products a year, with South Korea a relatively small market taking A$26 million worth in 1995/96.
Australia exported A$148 million worth of beef to South Korea in 1995/96. Total Australian beef and veal exports in that year were worth A$2.38 billion.
There were no signs of Japanese market nerves over Australian dairy and meat products because of the anthrax outbreak, a spokesman for Fischer told Reuters.
Anthrax is a bacteria disease which causes rapid death in cattle and sheep but which generally does not affect humans. It cannot be caught through consumption of processed dairy products.
Ausatralian meat exports from the anthrax-affected area were stopped when the outbreak was first discovered in Januuary.
